title: Cap. V Obj. 2 Sol close: crass error — God never bound himself Si prius credideris, licebit praedestinare
pass_a_gloss: It is therefore a crass error to opine that that first and eternal destination of some singular person by God to life is bound by the same laws by which the temporal attainment as to the men themselves is bound. For the same God who said this law to man, If you shall have believed, I will give you life, or you will be saved, never imposed this law on himself, If you shall first have believed, it will be lawful for me to predestinate you to life; otherwise it will by no means be lawful.
pass_b_english: So it is a crass error to think that God's first eternal destinating of a singular person to life is bound by the same laws that bind temporal attainment on the human side. The same God who told man, If you believe, I will give you life — or you will be saved — never bound himself: If you first believe, then I may predestinate you to life; otherwise I may not.
source_text: Crassus igitur error est opinari, primam illam et aeternam personae alicujus singularis a Deo ad vitam destinationem iisdem legibus adstrictam, quibus temporalis consecutio quoad ipsos homines adstricta est. Idem enim Deus qui homini hanc legem dixit, Si credideris, dabo tibi vitam, vel salvus eris, nunquam hanc legem sibi imposuit, Si prius credideris, licebit mihi te praedestinare ad vitam; secus haud licebit.
